# Check — M0-d-03, `dmath`: `pow`, `log`, `exp`, `sin`, `cos`, `atan2`, `atan`, ported from fdlibm 5.3 (lane check/M0-d-03, 2026-10-03)

**Verdict: PASS. Every line of M0.md §3's checklist passes. One note (N-1) records three test-strength gaps in the
known-answer vectors. They are not failing lines: the port is right on all three paths, as the checker's independent runs
show.**

* **The exit bar holds (CONFIRMED).** "Known-answer tests pass on Node arm64 and under Rosetta": `kat-hosts.mjs` reports
  every case of all 7 routines bit-identical on Node arm64 and on Node x64 under Rosetta 2, against both vector sets. The
  checker's own step also passes. `gen.sh --check` recompiles the C harness for arm64 and x86-64, regenerates both sets,
  and finds them byte-identical to each other and to the committed files. The 17 netlib files' SHA-256 equal their
  `CLEAN-ROOM.md` §5 rows P-0002 – P-0018.
* **Every gate exits 0**, and `probe-red` names all ten planted lines. The item's 39 tests are green at the PR size and
  at 2 × 10⁵ runs. The kernel project passes 126 / 126 and the tools project 207 / 207.
* **The port matches fdlibm's C beyond the committed vectors (CONFIRMED).** The checker built its own C oracle from the
  vendored sources with the item's flags. It ran 602 954 fresh arguments (a new seed and new families) on both
  architectures, and 5 242 880 sin / cos arguments within 2 ulp of n·π/2 for n = 1 … 524 288. That is e_rem_pio2's
  whole medium range, where its second and third Cody–Waite iterations act. All runs gave 0 misses. A line-by-line read
  against the C found no difference. Every constant equals its hexadecimal comment (97) and its C literal (68 named
  scalars, 10 arrays, the 66-entry `two_over_pi` and the 32-entry `npio2_hw`).
* **Of the checker's 22 mutants, 10 turn the item's KAT red.** Of the 12 survivors, 8 are equivalent or
  near-equivalent (reasoned below). The other 4 are real gaps in the vectors, not in the code. The checker's
  differential kills 3 of them; the fourth is killed only by the near-n·π/2 run. Together they are note N-1.

The checker seat is check/M0-d-03 (Opus, on the owner's Mac). It is independent of build/M0-d-03. Its ledger row is
L-0037. Receipts are in the session scratchpad (`waves/chk-d03-*.log`, `waves/chk-d03/`). The machine was shared with
other wave-2 seats and M-1's research-side seats, so no timing is taken or judged here.

## The checker's independent runs (CONFIRMED, scratch `waves/chk-d03/`; nothing in `plat/` written)

* **Oracle.** `oracle.c` reads `routine hex [hex]` lines and prints fdlibm's result bits, with NaN made canonical as in
  C-0135 (1). It was built against `plat/vendor/fdlibm-5.3/` with the item's flags
  (`-O0 -ffp-contract=off -fno-fast-math -fno-builtin -D__LITTLE_ENDIAN -w`), once with `-arch arm64` and once with
  `-arch x86_64`.
* **Fresh-argument differential** (`diff.mjs`; dmath bundled from `plat/packages/kernel/src/dmath/index.ts`; seed
  mulberry32, not the item's splitmix64). The families: any bit pattern; magnitudes up to 2¹⁰²³; sin and cos within
  3 ulp of n·π/2 for n ≤ 2 × 10⁶; 6381956970095103 · 2ᵏ for k = 0 … 960; exp's subnormal, overflow and tiny ranges; log
  near 1 and over subnormals; atan and atan2 on wide ranges; pow on ranges, negative x with integer y, near-one x with
  huge y, subnormal x, and the exact boundaries y · log₂ x = 1024 and −1075. The result: `cases 602954 (sin 101922,
  cos 100961, exp 80000, log 80000, atan 60000, atan2 60000, pow 120071); misses 0` against `oracle-arm64` on Node
  arm64, and the same line against `oracle-x86_64` on Node x64 under Rosetta 2.
* **The medium reduction range** (`hard.mjs`). sin and cos at every double within 2 ulp of n·π/2, n = 1 … 524 288:
  `near n·π/2: 5242880 cases, misses 0`.
* **Coverage** (`cov.mjs`; the item's own `kat-run.ts` under `NODE_V8_COVERAGE`). The committed vectors execute every
  block of `src/dmath/` except 11. Seven of the 11 cannot be reached from dmath's callers:
  * scalbn's input of zero or a subnormal, its NaN / ∞ return, and its overflow and underflow returns, with `copysign`
    (pow and the large reduction pass only normal values with moderate exponents);
  * remPio2's |x| ≤ π/4 and non-finite branches (sin and cos return before calling it);
  * kernelRemPio2's `jv < 0` clamp (`(e0 − 3) / 24` truncates to 0 for every e0 ≥ −3 it receives);
  * the big-endian side of the word probe.

  Two of the 11 can be reached: pow's exact-boundary branches at `pow.ts:245` (z = 1024) and `pow.ts:253` (z = −1075).
  These are N-1 (a).
* **Lint bite** (`lintmut.mjs`; `exp.ts`'s text linted in memory at its own path). As landed: `clean`. With one
  vetted-division directive removed: `78:plat/ratio-division`. With `Math.exp` planted: `76:plat/math-allowlist`. So
  the sixteen directives are load-bearing, and the folder is linted under the model rule set.
* **C-0137's measured bounds re-measured** (dmath bundle, 10⁶ – 3 × 10⁶ draws per range). The worst `exp(log x)` error
  is 1 ulp on [1/e, e], 1 on [1/4, 4], 2 on [1/16, 16] and 4 on [2⁻¹⁰, 2¹⁰]. The worst |sin² + cos² − 1| is 1 · 2⁻⁵²
  over magnitudes 2⁻¹⁰⁵⁰ – 2¹⁰⁵⁰. Both reproduce C-0137 (1) and (2).

## Notes (not failing lines)

**N-1 — three reachable paths that the committed vectors do not distinguish (test strength; the code is right on all
three).**

* **(a) pow's exact overflow and underflow boundaries.** These are `pow.ts:245` (z = y · log₂ x exactly 1024) and
  `pow.ts:253` (exactly −1075). No vector reaches either branch (coverage), so mutants M1 and M2, which swap ±∞ and 0
  there, keep the KAT green. fdlibm and dmath agree on, for example, pow(2, 1024) = +∞, pow(4, 512) = +∞,
  pow(−2, 1025) = −∞, pow(2, −1075) = +0 and pow(0.5, 1075) = +0, and on all 120 071 pow cases of the checker's
  differential.
* **(b) pow's odd-integer test for an integer |y| in [2²¹, 2⁵³) whose low word is at least 2³¹, with x < 0**
  (`pow.ts:102`, which needs `lo()` unsigned, `words.ts:24`). M22, a signed `lo()`, keeps the KAT green: the
  vectors' large-integer y are 2⁵² + (below 2²⁰), whose low words stay below 2³¹. For example,
  pow(−(1 + 2⁻⁵²), 2⁵² + 2³¹ + 1) is −2.7182831246371366 in fdlibm and in dmath (`c005bf0b390cae7a`), and NaN under M22.
* **(c) e_rem_pio2's third Cody–Waite iteration** (`rem-pio2.ts:319`). The vectors execute it, but no committed
  argument changes bits when it is removed (M14). Of the 5 242 880 doubles within 2 ulp of n·π/2 (n ≤ 524 288), 71 do,
  for example sin(`41065a1dd290660f`), sin(`40ffe9e875a67a0b`) and cos(`40f6d9be62d85044`). dmath matches fdlibm on all
  of them.
* Two of the item's descriptions say more than the vectors do. `gen/kat.c` line 141 says 6381956970095103 exercises
  "e_rem_pio2's 3rd iteration and k_rem_pio2". That argument is above 2¹⁹ · π/2, so it takes only k_rem_pio2.
  C-0135 (4) and the vectors' README say "each routine's branch thresholds", which does not hold for (a).

*Suggested for any later fix round of the item; it does not block:* add three families to `gen/kat.c` and regenerate
both sets with `gen.sh`:

* the pairs y · log₂ x = 1024 and −1075 for x = ±2ᵏ;
* negative x with integer y = 2⁵² + 2³¹ + j and 2⁴⁰ + 2³¹ + j;
* the doubles near n·π/2 that need the third iteration (the checker's `waves/chk-d03/hard.mjs` finds them).

Then correct the two sentences, by a new choices row and the comment. M1, M2, M14 and M22 then turn red under the KAT.

**N-2 — for M0-d-06 (cross-host) and any later dmath reader.** dmath's KAT runs on Node arm64 and on x64 under Rosetta.
The browsers and workers are M0-d-06's legs, as C-0135 (5) says, and `kat-run.ts`'s `runKat(root)` is the check that
M0-d-06 can bundle. τ's one rounding above e_hi is left by C-0137 (4) to M0-b-02: §4.6 states τ ∈ [e_lo, e_hi], and the
stage clamps if it needs the closed range.

## Not done, and why

* **netlib was not re-fetched.** The comparison of the vendored bytes with netlib's live files would download 17 files.
  The checker seat downloads nothing without the owner's say-so in the chat. The vendored files are checked against the
  author's recorded SHA-256 (all equal) and read in full.
* **No browser or worker leg.** That is M0-d-06's, by the brief.
